promises.title: Notes remain authoritative
promises.guarantee: Visual authoring never replaces the note field as the canonical project data.

promises.title: Unknown syntax is preserved
promises.guarantee: Unsupported tags, comments, whitespace, casing, and handwritten prose must survive unchanged.

promises.title: Syntax goes to the correct surface
promises.guarantee: Database notes, map notes, event notes, page comments, commands, routes, and text codes are never conflated.

promises.title: Installed source wins
promises.guarantee: Generated syntax is validated against the plugin version actually present in the user's project whenever available.

promises.title: No YEP source redistribution
promises.guarantee: Playroma ships independently written metadata, hashes, and short syntax schemas, never YEP JavaScript or copied help files.

promises.title: Bundle normalization is deterministic
promises.guarantee: The same source bundle produces the same canonical plugin selection and metadata apart from the report timestamp.

promises.title: Conflicts are explicit
promises.guarantee: Differing files with the same plugin filename require a recorded resolution and may not be silently collapsed.

promises.title: Every supplied plugin is classified
promises.guarantee: Each unique plugin receives at least one coverage mode, even when its only role is configuration or runtime validation.

promises.title: Dependencies carry evidence
promises.guarantee: Dependency edges record their source location and whether they are hard requirements or feature-specific integrations.

promises.title: The framework stays provider-neutral
promises.guarantee: Yanfly is the first provider; core contracts must not prevent later Olivia, Irina, VisuStella, or custom catalogs.

promises.title: All future edits are undoable
promises.guarantee: Every generated metadata change must integrate with Playroma's command and undo infrastructure.

promises.title: Lunatic code is not trusted
promises.guarantee: JavaScript and formula blocks are never executed in the editor process and are validated only in an isolated sandbox.

phase0ExitConditions: The supplied archive is normalized into unique plugin records and source occurrences.
Versions and SHA-256 fingerprints are recorded without copying plugin source.
Exact and conflicting duplicates are distinguished.
Every plugin has authoring-surface signals and at least one coverage mode.
An initial evidence-backed dependency graph is generated.
Known conflicting duplicates have explicit canonical resolutions.
A machine-readable golden inventory and human-readable audit report are checked in.
Automated tests enforce counts, resolution rules, classification completeness, and licensing boundaries.
